v:I give my feelings
a shape,
give them a body,
and let them wander among you.
In them
there may be
merits,
flaws,
faults .............. anything.
I accept them all,
from the very first seed

Raji sat at the entrance of the hill temple. The beauty of nature all around enchanted her.. Raji sat there, forgetting she had come for darshan. Suddenly, as if she had remembered, she turned to look. Amritha was nowhere to be seen. She got up and searched all around. There she was, running and playing under the peepal tree.
"Amritha. Come here! Can't you see there are monkeys up there? Didn't I tell you to stay next to me? Why did you come here, darling!" There was a little of the anger of searching in her voice.
Damming her anger and standing as a shield for Amritha, Bala came along. "I went a little way over there. Has she already caused a fuss!" said Bala.
In the middle of this exchange, Amritha, frightened by her mother's scolding, tried to reach for her father's hands; she couldn't. She hugged his legs tightly instead,
"Why did you go off and leave me alone? And it's a new place. Do you know I got scared? How many times have I told you. If you're going, tell me before you go"
"Can I always be with you, Raji? One day you'll have to learn to be alone too," Bala said, laughing.

Anger welled up inside Raji. "Can't you talk about anything else in a temple? We'll have our quarrel later; first we have to finish the archanai and leave. Only if we leave now will there be time to cook the rice for lunch," and as Raji hurried ahead, Bala picked up Amritha and followed.
The house was in some sort of uproar
"Sindhu! Did you see that file?" Aadhi shouted from inside the room.
"Wait a minute. Look properly. Should I watch the stove here, or watch you?"
Mangalam sat in the hall watching all this like a show. Even her spectacles wouldn't stay put and kept slipping down her nose. That's how old she was.
"Got the file! I'm off, Sindhu!" said Aadhi, and started to leave without waiting for her reply.
As he went, as if he had remembered something, he said, "Amma! I'm off!"
Mangalam said, "Go safely, pa." He didn't even stay until her smile had faded. She ended that smile in disappointment. And he set off and was gone.
Sindhu came out too, with her bag.
"Mami! I've made the food.. I've done lunch as well. It's in the hot box. Help yourself. If it's gone cold ........ wait a minute, Mami," she said, and wrote something on a slip of paper.

"Mami, I'm leaving this slip here. You know the girl who usually comes to clean the house. Show it to her. She'll heat it up for you. Is everything all right, Mami?!" she said, and got ready to leave.
"Sindhu …………………… one minute!"
"What, Mami ………………, what do you need?"
"Sindhu …………………….I meant to ask you yesterday……………….you'd both gone to sleep .....................will you drop me at the temple today on your way to work, dear? …………………...I'll come back by myself"
Only then did Sindhu notice that Mangalam was all dressed in a sari and ready.

"What, Mami? Since we came to this town you haven't even gone out anywhere! There aren't many of our people in this town either. And you don't know the language! How can I send you alone, Mami ……………………….what's special today?....................Some Shashti or Chathurthi or something?"
"No, Sindhu dear ...today is his birthday ..."

Sindhu didn't know what to say. Aadhi's father had passed away only recently. It was after that, for a change, that Aadhi got a transfer and came here with the family. Since coming here, Mangalam hadn't wanted to go out anywhere. Today, when for the first time she asked Sindhu to go out, Sindhu couldn't refuse.

"Wait a minute, Mami. I'll tell the office I'm taking leave and come," she said, and went inside. A glow came over Mangalam's face that hadn't been there till then. But Sindhu wasn't there to notice it.
Having finished the archanai, Raji came down slowly. Ahead of her, Bala hurried down carrying Amritha.
"Carrying a grown-up child like that. Shameful. Shameful. Put her down!" Raji shouted. Bala went on as if none of it had reached his ears.
"Hey Raji. You're Raji, aren't you!" Sindhu asked, seeing Raji coming down, shouting at someone below.
"Sindhu? What are you doing here?" she asked, raising her eyebrows in surprise.
"I should be asking you that. This is my town now. How come you're here?" Sindhu teased her with mock severity.
"Oh, that…………….. I've just moved house to this town," Raji said, smiling.

"How long it's been since I saw you. The last time I came to see your baby. You got married before all of us and even became a mother. After that we never saw each other in person. Not on Facebook either. You quietly escaped somewhere!"
Raji said, laughing, "I lived just 5 or 6 streets from your mother's house. If you'd wanted to, you could have taken four steps and come to see me"

"Where did I get the time, di? So much work there was .. ..oh my ..anyway, leave it ..oh ..sorry. Mami, this is my school friend. Her name is Raji. Raji, this is my mami. Aadhi's mother. You know Aadhi, don't you!"
"Oh! I know him well," said Raji, smiling.
"Mami, you go on up to the temple. I'll chat with her a little and come"
"All right, dear……. you chat and come," said Mangalam, and went up.
"Come, Raji! Come and sit on the step here ………So where's your husband? Bala's his name, isn't it? You've got a girl, haven't you, her name's ... ..."
"Amritha"
"Ah... Amritha.... I remember. Where are they……… going on ahead? Were you shouting at them as you came down? Oh no, I didn't look properly!" As Sindhu fretted, Raji gave only a smile in reply.
"Raji. Give me your home address. I'll come and see you if I can"
"If you can? You'll come and see me this week. Message me your address too."
"My goodness!... Raji, at school you hardly spoke to anyone. You never talked this much even to me. When did you change like this?
Raji laughed. "Can you stay the way you were at school? Everyone's time comes. Then you have to change"
"What, di? You're talking like a great sage"
Raji laughed
"That laugh. That alone hasn't changed at all. Do you know how beautiful you look when you laugh?"
Raji laughed again.
"This is my number. Note it down. Give me a missed call. I'll send the address. I've left Mami alone up there. We'll talk later," and with the exchange of numbers Sindhu flew back up.
When Raji came down, Bala was standing waiting for her.
"My school friend. Sindhu. She lives in this town, apparently. So I stopped to chat"
"So you've found a friend to talk to. Now you'll forget both of us!"
"Is that something to joke about? Go on, first. It's late!!" Raji said, and walked on.
"Mami! You've been out ....go and lie down and rest. You were coughing a bit even coming down the hill. Shall I call the doctor?"
"I climbed a hill after so many days, didn't I. That's all ......Sindhu ......at the temple, Amirtham who used to live near our old house...." Mangalam began,
"Mami. I only told the office half day ......it's getting late ...........I have to go..................I'll put on some songs on the radio............... listen and sleep," Sindhu interrupted.
Mangalam didn't hide the disappointment on her face. But Sindhu didn't understand it either.
When Sindhu went and turned on the radio, it began to play.
(An old film song plays, a woman singing that she wants to fly away but has no wings, that she longs to speak her heart but cannot find the words.)
"It's a very old song. Shall I put some Raja songs on the speaker, Mami?"
"No, dear, this is enough," said Mangalam, and drifted off.
"Raji, how did you find the house!!" Sindhu asked, seeing Raji standing at the door.

"Why, di....... did you think I was such an old almanac? There's the phone, isn't there. And it's not far …………. My house is just a kilometre away. The map told me. So I thought I'd just come and see you"
"Come in ..come and sit. One minute, I'll submit an office file and come"
Raji sat down.
Hearing that Raji had come, Mangalam opened her door and looked. Raji looked at Mangalam too.
Something at the corner of Mangalam's eyes seemed familiar to Raji
"Are you Sindhu's friend, dear?"
"Yes, Aunty"
By then Sindhu had come back
"Mami. Why did you come out? Such a fever you had last night. I got scared too. The doctor has said he's coming today. Go and rest, Mami"
Mangalam went back in without saying anything.
"What's wrong with Aunty?"
"She went out yesterday after a long time. She has asthma too. The cold wind must have got to her. That's why I've taken leave from the office and I'm staying home to look after Mami"
"Where's Aadhi?"
"He's gone to the office. Anyway. Leave that. Why didn't you bring Bala and Amritha?"
"Bala...well ..his father isn't well, so he's gone back home to the village"
"Amritha?"
"She's her daddy's pet. She said she'd go too and went"
Raji went on.
"Sindhu, don't you have kids yet?"
"No, di! We need to get ahead in our careers. We've put it off for a while," she said, and blushed. Raji knew why she blushed too.
"What, di, there are hardly any houses around. Your house stands all on its own. Aren't you scared?"
"No, di. Not really scared. If you go a bit further down this lane there's a big house, isn't there. You'd have passed it on the way?"
"Yes!"
"Ah ……………..that's some big officer's house, apparently. There's even a watchman for that house. So ...thieves and the like won't easily come this way"
"That's true. But don't you get bored on your own?"

"Where ..........if he and I go to the office, it's night by the time we get home. It's only Mami at home. She doesn't talk to anyone much either. Very much the silent type. After Mama passed, all the relatives coming would have been a disturbance, so we came to this town only last year"
"Doesn't your mami get bored on her own?"
"Che. She never talks much to anyone, ever. She keeps to herself with a book in her hand. That's what she likes"
Raji said nothing
"All right, I'll be off, Sindhu ..come to my place another day if you can!"
"OK, di…………….. shut the door when you go. I've got a bit of work inside!" said Sindhu, and went in
Before leaving, Raji peeped into the room where Mangalam was
Mangalam wasn't asleep. She was sitting on the cushioned bed in the middle of the room, looking at the window
Mangalam was comfortable there. Raji could see that at a glance. But there was also some emptiness there. It was in Mangalam's heart too.
As if she had thought of something, Raji went back in to see Sindhu
There, Sindhu was typing in a great hurry in front of the computer
Raji quietly shut the door and went out
Sindhu pressed the calling bell and stood outside.
Raji came and opened the door. "Come, Sindhu. Come in!"
Sindhu came and sat on the sofa. There wasn't much happiness on her face
"What happened, Sindhu? You suddenly phoned and said you were coming over. Why are you so worried?"

"Mami hasn't been well for two days. Aadhi and I are both staying at home. We don't even know what happened. She was fine. Now she just lies there. I can't bear to look at her. It happened because I took her out, didn't it ....” As she said it, Sindhu began to sob.
Raji went to her at once, comforted her and gave her water
"....It was Aadhi who sent me out. He said if I stayed there I'd only blame myself and worry, go out for a bit. I also felt it would be good to talk to someone. So I came"
Raji said nothing. She stayed silent. She thought of saying something, then let it go.
"Why, Raji? Have I been a nuisance to you?"
"Che. Nothing like that. In a way it's good you came here. Bala and Amritha are on their way back. You kept saying you wanted to meet them, didn't you. You can meet them before you go"
"Is it! Sorry, di, I've spoiled your mood too"
"That's nothing, di. Shall I make you some tea?"
"Wait. I'll go and make the tea. You stay and see if they're coming."
"OK, di ..the kitchen's that way. He's labelled everything. Call if you need help. They'll be here any minute"
"OK!" said Sindhu, and went in and put the water on to boil
Sindhu heard Raji's cooing voice: "Amri darling ………come, come ……”
"Oh, they've come! I'll make tea for them too and take it out," Sindhu thought, and came out carrying the tea.
"Bala, go and have a bath. Why has Amritha got so thin? Wasn't the food good at Mama's place?"
"Bala, this is Sindhu. She kept saying she wanted to meet you. Amritha, say hi to Aunty!"
"Amritha, don't touch the toys now."
"Raji!!!!!! What game is this?" Sindhu shook her hard.
Only Sindhu and Raji were there. There was no one else. There never had been.
Raji stood still. Sindhu's eyes had filled with tears. Silence spoke there. Sindhu looked at Raji. Raji looked at Sindhu. In that instant, laughter and tears came and went by turns on Raji's face.
"Raji..what are you doing..what..why?.."
"You said I never used to talk at school. See how I talk now," she laughed mockingly.
Sindhu didn't speak

"What are you staring at, di? Thinking I'm mad? Don't worry. I know too that this isn't real. I haven't got so bad that I can't tell what's real from what's a shadow," said Raji, wiping her face, and she took the tray from Sindhu and went into the kitchen. Sindhu followed like a wind-up doll

"A car accident.... it turned my whole life upside down. Lots of people came. They gave money. They found me a house. They consoled me, they said no one should ever have to suffer like this. Everyone fell over themselves to look after me. But none of them understood what I needed then"
"It's true I grieved that Bala and Amritha were gone. You can cry that out. I'm still doing that, to this day. But beyond that there was another pain
Sindhu looked at her as if to ask, "What?"

"Emptiness. You can't say in words what it's like. I lost something that was inside me. For that, all I needed was one living soul to talk to out loud with me. The thought that every day someone is thinking of me too! But nobody understood that!! I can't blame anyone either. Because of this hurried world. Once I too went along at that same hurry. But when I stopped, no one stopped with me. Everyone kept going past me. Even now I'm still standing there, Sindhu ...like your mami .."
Raji's eyes welled up.

What Raji had acted out was not only the lesson of her own life. It was the remedy for Mangalam's longing. Sindhu understood that too. She stood silently looking at Raji for a minute. Then she picked up her bag and hurried out.
"Why, Raji, do you think she understood?" said Bala
"She understood. That's why she's going. But"
"But what?"
Raji peeped outside. Sindhu was walking fast. And behind Sindhu, Mangalam was walking along too.
note: Mami here means mother-in-law, and Mama father-in-law; "di" is an intimate form of address between women friends. An archanai is an offering of prayers made in someone's name at a temple.
